messages:
Taylor (PM): quick sync — we need to lock the rerank API knobs for next sprint. main items: input/output top_k semantics, candidate_weight handling, tie-breakers when truncating, and normalization options. want a spec + rollout checklist by Fri.

Alex C: ok. proposal idea: two params input_top_k (how many to evaluate) and output_top_k (how many to return). default behavior should match today for backward compat.

Maya R: agree on 2 knobs. implementation: input_top_k acts as a hard cap for evaluation unless partner opt-in disables truncation. if payload > input_top_k server will select which candidates to evaluate based on candidate_weight * submission_priority (if provided) then stable index tie-breaker.

Raj P: stable ordering is important for caches. tie-breaker order: client_id if present, else candidate.id, else original index. log an event when we truncate and include truncated_count in response metadata.

Alex C: weights: accept optional candidate_weight float on each candidate. runtime multiplies model logit by weight before calibration+normalization. if absent default=1. example payload:

```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"c_23","text":"...","candidate_weight":0.6},
    {"id":"c_24","text":"..."}
  ],
  "input_top_k": 75,
  "output_top_k": 10,
  "normalize": "softmax" // enum: "none" | "minmax" | "softmax"
}
```

Maya R: normalization default should be softmax post-calibration. note: cross-model comparability requires per-model calibration parameters (scale + offset) applied to logits before normalization. we'll ship a small calibration table in the model registry and update it as models change.

Taylor (PM): what about clients wanting absolute score ranges (0..1) so they can combine with their features?

Maya R: min-max normalization can be an option but needs stable historical bounds. recommend softmax default and minmax as opt-in when client supplies expected bounds or after we provide calibrated ranges.

Raj P: truncation metadata: include truncated_by_server (bool), truncated_count, truncation_policy ("by_weight"|"by_order"), and truncation_seed if we need reproducibility for debugging.

Alex C: backward compatibility: defaults: input_top_k = number of candidates received, output_top_k = min(10, candidates), normalize=softmax. also add header X-Rerank-API-Version with value "v2" once rolled out. we'll gate with an opt-in header during beta.

Taylor (PM): rollout checklist draft:
- spec PR merged + changelog
- server impl + unit tests for truncation & tie-breakers
- calibration table + offline calibration job
- SDK changes + examples in Python/TS
- telemetry: events for truncation, avg candidates evaluated, model-used, latency
- beta for 2 weeks with opt-in header + feature flag
- perf target: p95 latency <= baseline * 1.15 for median 50-candidate workloads
- cost target: tokens_evaluated_per_request <= 1.25x baseline when input_top_k unset
- migration guide / samples

Maya R: I'll own server work and calibration job. target to have tests by Wed.

Alex C: SDK + examples owned by me. I'll add sample showing using candidate_weight and reading response metadata.

Raj P: I'll add telemetry schema and a partner-only flag to disable truncation for a small set of customers for validation. also add logs for tie-breaker decisions.

SRE Bot: feature-flag: created rerank.input_output_topk_experiment :white_check_mark: — rollout controls in place.

Taylor (PM): good. I'll write the public-facing spec and opt-in beta instructions and file PR. sync Friday 10am for pre-rollout review. if anyone strongly objects to normalization default or tie-breaker order speak up now.

Alex C: no objections. small note: we should document how weights interact with model probability outputs in the SDK README.

Maya R: agreed. will add inline comments in spec about calibration interplay.

Raj P: fine from infra side. will surface truncation events to ops dashboard.

Taylor (PM): thanks team — filing spec PR now.
